goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration queries for embed_category and uncategorized_category_id site settings crash with NoMethodError on nil because default-only settings are not materialized as DB rows, breaking fresh installs
Migration inserts interpolated host values directly into SQL without sanitization, causing PG syntax errors on hosts containing single quotes

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration builds raw SQL with `execute "... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, directly interpolating each host string `h` into a single-quoted SQL literal. If any existing `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` line contains a single quote, the SQL becomes invalid (PG syntax error). This is also unsafe vs SQL injection in general; it should use parameterization/quoting (e.g., `quote(h)` or `insert` helpers).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update calls methods on nil when the host id doesn't exist, causing a 500 instead of a 404
Admin::EmbeddableHostsController destroy action raises NoMethodError on nil host, returning a 500 instead of 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy`. If no record matches the given `id`, `host` will be `nil`, and calling `destroy` will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 rather than a 404/not-found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that never reads params or mutates anything, silently discarding future user input with a 200 response

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` after `fetch_embedding` and never reads `params` or persists any changes, so a `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` will return 200 with the current embedding data regardless of input. The current UI mostly manages hosts via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, and the template doesn’t call `saveChanges`, so this is more an incomplete/placeholder endpoint than a user-visible defect in the diff as shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: saveChanges action in admin-embedding.js.es6 is dead code not triggered by any template, and the PUT customize/embedding route forms an inert feature

adjudication.rationale: In the new admin UI, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines a `saveChanges()` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, but `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` never invokes `saveChanges` (it only renders per-host rows and an `addHost` button). Separately, the PR adds `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, but `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not persist any changes (it just re-serializes `@embedding`), so even if called it would be a no-op. This looks like unused/incomplete plumbing rather than a directly user-visible defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddableHostsController update and destroy don't nil-check EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, so a nonexistent id causes a 500 NoMethodError instead of a 404
Migration interpolates host values into raw INSERT SQL, risking broken inserts or SQL injection; should use parameterized exec_insert

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration loops over `records.each do |h|` and runs `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. This directly interpolates the host string into SQL without escaping/parameterization, so a host containing `'` (or other SQL metacharacters) can break the migration and could allow SQL injection via crafted `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddingController#update renders the serializer without reading params and mutates nothing, so frontend saveChanges is silently discarded — the endpoint is inert

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without reading `params` or persisting anything (and `@embedding` is an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`). So the endpoint is effectively a no-op. However, the UI changes in this diff save host changes via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (`host.save(props)` / `destroyRecord()`), and `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` does not invoke the controller’s `saveChanges` action at all. So while the finding is accurate about the update action being inert if called, it’s not clearly a user-facing broken behavior in this diff—more an incomplete/unused endpoint/action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost model lacks a uniqueness validation on host and the migration adds no unique index, allowing duplicates that make record_for_host's .first silently ignore category edits

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` the only validation on `host` is `validates_format_of`; there is no `validates :host, uniqueness: ...`. The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates `embeddable_hosts` without any unique index on `host`. Lookup uses `record_for_host` → `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so if duplicates exist (which the schema/validations allow), the chosen record (and thus `category_id` used in `TopicEmbed.import`) becomes order-dependent and can silently ignore the intended category for that host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs for embeddable_hosts and embedding are placeholder 'is a subclass' assertions with zero request coverage of create/update/destroy, authorization, validation errors, category fallback, or serialization

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial admin controllers (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController with create/update/destroy and save_host logic incl. uncategorized fallback; Admin::EmbeddingController show/update and serialization of hosts). However, the newly added controller specs (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) only assert the classes subclass Admin::AdminController and do not exercise any requests, authorization constraints, validation/error paths, category_id fallback behavior, or rendered JSON/serialization. This is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic#expandable_first_post? drops the 'no hosts configured' guard while the spec 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' now passes for the wrong reason and no longer tests what its name claims; topics with lingering TopicEmbed will render expandable

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`, removing any “hosts configured” gating (app/models/topic.rb). The updated spec still has an example named “is false if embeddable_host is blank”, but it no longer sets `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` or stubs `has_topic_embed?`, so it will pass simply because the default `embed_truncate` setting is false, not because there are no `EmbeddableHost` records (spec/models/topic_spec.rb). This is a real, diff-grounded test/expectation mismatch and suggests a missing guard based on `EmbeddableHost` presence, but whether the behavior change is definitively a product bug (vs intentional) can’t be proven from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No JS test coverage for the new admin embedding UI (embeddable-host component, admin-embedding controller, pathFor adapter), leaving the fragile hand-rolled save/state sync flow untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new admin embedding UI surface in Ember (e.g., `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6`, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`, `admin/routes/admin-embedding.js.es6`, and the `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` component + templates). The component contains nontrivial, stateful behavior (buffered edits, `editToggled`, focus scheduling, save/delete/cancel flows with `host.save(props)` and `destroyRecord()`), but the only JS tests added/modified are for the generic store embedded hydration (`test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6`) and pretender fixtures. There are no new QUnit/acceptance/component tests exercising the new admin embedding route/controller/component/adapter, so the finding about missing JS test coverage is supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration copies embeddable_hosts setting values raw into the new table without model normalization (scheme stripping), breaking embed requests for hosts stored with http(s):// prefixes
Migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when the embed_category setting is unset because it calls .to_i on the result of a query that may return no rows

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `category_id = execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i`. If the query for `embed_category` returns no rows, `execute(...)[0]` will be `nil`, and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError` before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. This matches the finding about crashing when the setting is unset/missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin EmbeddingController update action is a no-op that discards parameters yet returns success, while the frontend pretends to save changes

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action ignores any incoming params and simply re-renders `@embedding` (an `OpenStruct` built in `fetch_embedding`), so it does not persist changes despite being exposed as `PUT /admin/customize/embedding`. On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`, which would hit that no-op endpoint. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not invoke `saveChanges` or present a save UI, and actual host changes are persisted via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, so this is more of an API/UX semantics concern than a demonstrable broken behavior in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController destroy and update actions raise NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 when the host id is not found

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record exists, `host` is `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)`, where `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...` and `host.category_id = ...`, causing a `NoMethodError` on `nil`. `destroy` does `host.destroy` on `nil`, also raising `NoMethodError`. The diff shows no not-found handling (e.g., `find`, `find_by!`, or explicit 404), so missing ids would result in a 500 rather than a 404.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Generic store _hydrateEmbedded plural branch inserts false entries into hydrated arrays when a subtype can't be resolved, unlike the singular path

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, the new plural `_id(s?)` branch maps IDs via `_lookupSubType` and assigns the resulting array directly (`obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`). Unlike the singular branch (which only assigns when `hydrated` is truthy), the plural branch does not filter out unresolved lookups, so missing embedded records will produce arrays containing `undefined`/falsy entries (and `hydrated || []` is ineffective since `map` always returns an array). This matches the finding that the plural path can insert falsey entries when a subtype can't be resolved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removing SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? check from expandable_first_post? silently changes first-post expansion behavior for sites without embeddable hosts

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/topic.rb`, `expandable_first_post?` previously required `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` in addition to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`, but the diff removes that gating check. As a result, if `embed_truncate` is enabled and a topic has an existing embed (`has_topic_embed?` true), the first-post expansion can now be enabled even when there are no configured/allowed embeddable hosts (now represented by `EmbeddableHost` records). This is a silent behavior change for installations without embeddable hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category fabricator and embeddable_host fabricator file contents are swapped, misplacing all category fabricator definitions

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the contents are effectively swapped: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `Fabricator(:category)` and related category variants. This is a real, diff-grounded issue (misnamed/misplaced definitions) that can confuse maintenance and could break setups that require fabricators by filename, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes failing behavior if all fabricators are auto-required.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration interpolates admin-entered host values raw into INSERT SQL (breaking on quotes) and uses change with no reversible path for the data migration
Port-bearing hosts never match: write path stores host:port but record_for_host compares against port-stripped uri.host, defeating the allowlist

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, `before_validation` strips scheme and path but leaves an entered port intact (e.g. `example.com:3000`). `record_for_host` then parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`; `uri.host` excludes the port. As a result, a stored `host` containing `:port` will never match lookups/allow checks, so port-bearing allowlist entries won’t work as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case drift: stored host is not lowercased on write while the query lowercases only the column, so mixed-case hosts fail to match
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments describe the same case-insensitive matching bug: the query applies LOWER() only to the stored host/column but the compared value (parameter/host being looked up) is not normalized, so mixed-case hosts may not match as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update and destroy in EmbeddableHostsController crash with NoMethodError when params[:id] doesn't resolve, returning 500 instead of 404

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without handling the not-found case. If no record matches, `host` is `nil`, and `save_host(host)` calls `host.host = ...` (NoMethodError) and `host.destroy` in `destroy` also raises, resulting in a 500 rather than a 404/handled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: before_validation self.host.sub! raises NoMethodError on nil host, so a missing host param produces a 500 instead of a validation error

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, the `before_validation` callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!(...)` twice. If `host` is `nil` (e.g., `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` missing in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`), `sub!` will raise `NoMethodError` before validations run, producing a 500 rather than a validation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PUT /admin/customize/embedding update action ignores the request body entirely and re-renders the unmodified record, silently discarding payloads

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, the `update` action does not read or apply any request parameters; it simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` after `fetch_embedding` builds an `OpenStruct` (`id: 'default', embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all...`). Given the route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`, any PUT payload would be ignored and effectively discarded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError when embed_category setting has no matching category, because execute(...)[0]['id'] assumes a row exists

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` when looking up the category from the `embed_category` site setting. If the SELECT returns zero rows (e.g., `embed_category` is unset/blank or doesn’t match any `categories.name`), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`, so `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError` before the later `category_id == 0` fallback can run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration lacks a unique index on host and an index on category_id, and interpolates raw setting values into SQL

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the insert statement interpolates the prior `site_settings` value directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. Since `h` comes from `val.split("\n")` and is not quoted/escaped, a host containing a `'` (or worse, crafted SQL) could break the migration or execute unintended SQL. Also, the table is created with no indexes/constraints (no unique index on `host`, no index on `category_id`), which is verifiable from the `create_table` block, though that part is more of a performance/data-integrity concern than the core defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-sargable lower(host) = ? query on the hottest read path with no index on embeddable_hosts.host, causing full table scans

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). The migration creating `embeddable_hosts` adds no index on `host` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb). Using `lower(host)` makes a normal index on `host` non-usable unless a functional index exists, so as written this can cause full table scans. This is a concrete performance concern on read paths that now call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (e.g., EmbedController#ensure_embeddable and TopicRetriever#invalid_host?).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unique constraint on host allows duplicate hosts, making record_for_host's .first return an arbitrary row

adjudication.rationale: The new `embeddable_hosts` table/migration (`create_table :embeddable_hosts`) adds no unique index/constraint on `host`, and the `EmbeddableHost` model has no `validates_uniqueness_of :host`. Yet lookup logic uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses that single row to pick the category (`eh.try(:category_id)`). If duplicate hosts are inserted (possible via the new admin CRUD controller), `.first` can select an arbitrary matching row (no ORDER BY), leading to inconsistent/incorrect category selection and host policy behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator file contents were swapped: category_fabricator.rb defines the embeddable_host fabricator and vice versa

adjudication_records.issue_text: _hydrateEmbedded plural branch can produce arrays of null entries, making the || [] guard dead code and crashing downstream lookups

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch (`/(.+)_id(s?)$/` with `m[2]`) does `obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and assigns the resulting array directly to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]`. If `_lookupSubType` returns `null/undefined` for some ids, this will indeed produce arrays containing null entries, and the `hydrated || []` fallback is effectively dead because `map` always returns a truthy array. However, the diff does not show any concrete downstream crash, nor that server responses can omit referenced embedded records; the added JS tests always include matching `colors` objects, so the alleged crash is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embedding is a fake OpenStruct model with an update route and saveChanges action that can never persist anything

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#fetch_embedding` builds `@embedding` as an `OpenStruct` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts` (no persistence-backed model), and `#update` simply re-renders the same serializer without applying or saving any params. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not invoke `saveChanges` or present any "save" UI for embedding-level settings, so this is more an incomplete/unused endpoint/action than a user-visible broken behavior in the shown UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: After save, the embeddable-host component's findById(categoryId) can return undefined when the server defaults to uncategorized, leaving client and server disagreeing on the category

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6#save`, the client sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` but then, after `host.save(props)`, unconditionally does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`. On the server, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` defaults `host.category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` when the incoming `category_id` is blank. For a new host (or if the chooser is left empty), `categoryId` can be `null`, so `findById(null)` will return `undefined`, leaving the client-side `host.category` inconsistent with the persisted/defaulted `category_id` returned by the server.

adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? dropped the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard, loosening the semantics from forum-embedding-enabled to topic-has-embed

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard in `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (`topic.rb` changes from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). adjudication_records.issue_text: expandable_first_post? in app/models/topic.rb:869 silently drops the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? condition, changing truncation semantics so sites with empty embeddable_hosts and embed_truncate enabled return expandable_first_post? == true for topics with embeds

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration raw-INSERTs old embeddable_hosts setting values without applying the model's before_validation scheme/path trimming, so values like 'https://example.com/1234' are stored verbatim and record_for_host never matches, silently breaking existing installs' embedding, with the source setting then DELETEd

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration INSERT interpolates #{h} unescaped, so a host value containing a quote aborts the migration

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration builds raw SQL with `execute "... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` value split by newlines. This interpolates `h` without escaping/quoting via the connection adapter, so a host string containing a single quote (or other SQL-special chars) would produce invalid SQL and can abort the migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController update action renders the serializer without reading or persisting params, and the front-end saveChanges sends an empty payload, making PUT /admin/customize/embedding a silent no-op endpoint that discards user input

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import derives the topic's category from the host record instead of the global embed_category setting, so URLs whose host has no EmbeddableHost row create topics with category: nil, falling to site default instead of the configured embed category

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the global `embed_category` site setting entirely (`config/site_settings.yml` and `server.en.yml`) and changes embedding access checks to require an `EmbeddableHost` row (`EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`). adjudication_records.issue_text: create_table :embeddable_hosts with force: true in a shipped migration drops any pre-existing table of that name, risking unrecoverable data loss

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates the table with `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it. If a pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` table exists (e.g., from an earlier/manual deployment or conflicting code), running this migration would irreversibly delete its contents, constituting a real data-loss risk grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Fabricator files' contents were swapped wholesale: category_fabricator.rb now contains the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb holds the category fabricators, severing git history and misleading future edits

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host returns false instead of nil on malformed URI, a truthiness trap for future callers refactoring host_allowed? to return the record

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`, `record_for_host` returns `false` on parse/host failures (`return false unless uri.present?` / `return false unless host.present?`) but otherwise returns an ActiveRecord object or `nil` (`where(...).first`). Current callers (`host_allowed?` uses `.present?`, and `TopicEmbed.import` uses `eh.try`) won’t break, so it’s not a demonstrated defect in this diff, but it’s a real API-contract concern grounded in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL string interpolation of untrusted embeddable_hosts setting value in migration can break the migration with single quotes; should use quote/parameterized insert

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host-allowlist matching is exact-string after lower() so trailing-dot referers or stored hosts with trailing dots never match, causing silent allow/deny drift; both sides should be normalized

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, the referer URL is parsed and matched via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` using `host = uri.host` with no normalization beyond whatever `URI()` returns (no stripping of a trailing dot). adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration uses create_table force: true for embeddable_hosts, silently dropping existing table and all host rows if re-run, causing irreversible data loss

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` does use `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which would drop and recreate the table if it already exists (e.g., if someone reruns the migration or the table was created out-of-band). However, as a newly added migration it is normally executed once on a fresh schema where the table does not exist, so this is not a guaranteed, immediate defect introduced by the PR; it’s a migration-safety/data-loss risk worth addressing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes on fresh installs when embed_category site setting is unset, because SELECT result nil.to_i raises NoMethodError, leaving partial schema with no transactional recovery on MySQL

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for the `embed_category` lookup. If the SELECT returns zero rows (plausible on fresh installs / when `embed_category` is unset), `execute(...)[0]` is `nil`, so `nil['id']` will raise `NoMethodError` before the subsequent `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. Because the `create_table` happens before this failing query, a crash can leave a partially-applied schema on DBs without transactional DDL (e.g., MySQL).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guard using embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0 is always falsy for SELECT in PostgreSQL, so the data migration never executes while the DELETE of site_settings runs unconditionally, destroying the allowlist

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, the code does `embeddable_hosts = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")` and then checks `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`. For a `SELECT`, `execute` returns a result set object (e.g., `PG::Result`), and `cmd_tuples` is not shown in the diff to be “always falsy”; it is commonly the row count for the result. So the claim that this guard will never pass (and therefore the migration “never executes”) is not verifiable from the diff and appears incorrect. While the `DELETE FROM site_settings ...` is unconditional, the asserted cause (cmd_tuples always falsy) is unsupported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts raw host setting values without the model's normalization (stripping scheme/path, downcasing), so migrated rows never match lookups and hosts are effectively dropped

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, old `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` entries are inserted via raw SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`) without running the `EmbeddableHost` model’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. But lookups later use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` which parses the URL and queries `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, i.e., it expects stored rows to be just the hostname. Any migrated rows that include scheme/path (which the old setting logic tolerated) will not match and will effectively be disallowed after migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw string interpolation of host values into INSERT SQL allows single quotes to corrupt the SQL, instead of using parameterized queries
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that host values are interpolated directly into an SQL INSERT string rather than using parameterized queries/quoting, creating SQL injection risk (and breaking SQL when quotes appear).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration has no rollback/down step to restore the deleted embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings, making the destructive cutover one-way with no expand/contract window

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses `def change` but performs irreversible data operations via `execute`, including `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`. There is no `down`/`reversible` logic to restore those settings or reverse the data copy, so rolling back the migration would be impossible or would lose the deleted setting values, making the cutover effectively one-way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Uncategorized fallback reads uncategorized_category_id from site_settings which may not exist as a persisted row, causing the same nil-crash on installs lacking that row

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration falls back to `execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i` when no `embed_category` match is found. If the SELECT returns zero rows (i.e., `uncategorized_category_id` is not persisted in `site_settings`), indexing `[0]` will be `nil` and `['value']` will raise, crashing the migration. There’s no presence/row-count guard around that fallback query.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddingController#update only re-renders the model without persisting changes, so admin save actions silently discard edits

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` does not read any params or persist anything; it just `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` (same as `show`). On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines a `saveChanges()` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which would issue a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` but the server ignores any changes. However, the provided template `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` does not expose a save button or any editable embedding settings besides embeddable hosts (which persist via `EmbeddableHost#save` hitting `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`). So the finding’s “silently discard edits” is not directly verifiable from the UI in this diff, but the `update` endpoint/action pair is indeed a no-op and potentially misleading/incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update/destroy in embeddable_hosts_controller raise NoMethodError (500) instead of 404 when the record doesn't exist

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then used without a nil check. If no record exists, `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` on `nil`, and `destroy` will call `host.destroy` on `nil`, both raising `NoMethodError` (500) instead of returning a 404/not found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update in embeddable_hosts_controller has same nil crash plus unconditionally overwrites host and category_id from params with no dirty check, allowing stale browser tab to clobber newer edits

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the record is fetched with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then passed to `save_host(host)`. If no record exists for that id, `host` will be `nil` and `save_host` will raise when it does `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...` (nil crash is directly verifiable from the diff). The “stale tab clobber newer edits” point is more about missing optimistic locking/dirty checks (not shown elsewhere), but the nil crash alone is a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: destroyRecord().then() in embeddable-host.js.es6 has no .catch, so delete failures are invisible to the admin

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... });` without any `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()`, which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the delete request fails, the rejection is unhandled and no error is shown to the admin, making failures effectively invisible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: saveChanges in admin-embedding.js.es6 calls a nonexistent update method on the store model, causing a runtime TypeError

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});` (admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6), but it does not show the implementation of the `embedding` client-side model returned by `this.store.find('embedding')` (admin/routes/admin-embedding.js.es6). Without the `Embedding` model code (or the base model class used by `store.find`) in the diff, it's not verifiable that `update` is nonexistent. Also, the new `embedding.hbs` template does not invoke `saveChanges`, so a runtime TypeError from this path is not demonstrated by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update action in embedding_controller.rb reports success while persisting nothing (re-renders serializer without reading params or saving)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without reading `params` or persisting anything. However, the diff also shows actual persistence for embedding configuration happening via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` (create/update/destroy of `EmbeddableHost`), and the Ember controller calls `embedding.update({})` with an empty payload. This makes the finding accurate as an endpoint/design concern (PUT exists but is effectively a no-op), but it’s not a clear functional defect given no other embedding-wide fields are introduced to be saved here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: plural hydration in store.js.es6 emits false entries when side-loaded records are missing, and the [] fallback is dead code, causing broken embedding table rows

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural branch for `*_ids` does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`. Since `Array#map` always returns an array (truthy) even when `_lookupSubType` returns `null/undefined`, this can emit arrays containing falsey entries when side-loaded records are missing, and the `|| []` fallback is effectively dead code. Downstream templates like `{{#each embedding.embeddable_hosts as |host|}}` could then iterate over `null/undefined` items, leading to broken rows/components.

adjudication_records.issue_text: no in-flight guard on save in embeddable-host.js.es6: Enter key can trigger overlapping PUTs, and category is set without committing the buffer leading to inconsistent rollback

adjudication.rationale: The component does have an in-flight guard: `cantSave` returns `isSaving || Ember.isEmpty(host)` and `save()` exits early if `this.get('cantSave')` is true, so once `host.save(props)` starts and `host.isSaving` flips true, subsequent Enter presses/clicks won’t trigger overlapping PUTs. Also, the claim about “category is set without committing the buffer leading to inconsistent rollback” isn’t verifiable from the diff: the only rollback path (`rollbackBuffer()`) is used on `cancel` for existing records, and after a successful save the UI exits editing (`editToggled=false`), so there’s no demonstrated inconsistent rollback behavior here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost queries in embedding_controller.rb run an uncached DB query on every embed request, adding per-request DB load on the hottest public embed path

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s `Admin::EmbeddingController` (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb) is an admin-only controller (routes under `/admin/customize/embedding`) and is not used on the public embed request path. The public embed check was changed in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` to call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`, which may query the DB per request, but that behavior is not coming from `embedding_controller.rb` as the finding claims.
